historical_context.time_period: The deep crisis, after industrial power has become load-bearing and before any stable contraction settlement.
historical_context.location: Brasswater Reserve House in the warm-sea terrace Hold served by Cistern House Nine, on the public counting gallery and connected lower freight-rail weighbridge.
historical_context.summary: A weekly reserve count becomes a public call-right hearing when a contracted Deep Company train arrives carrying mana-eating mould. The keeper can divert, hold, split, or release the shipment, but each path shifts cost among essential services, mine wages, export penalties, insurance, public credit, rail labour, and future deep-extraction debt.

public_facts.text: Brasswater is a public workshop with one civic seal, three reserve cells, a public service-days gauge, and an existing charter whose protected schedules and trigger cannot be altered by the keeper alone.
A call-right is an emergency diversion clause purchased through an earlier advance to a Deep Company; a winter warrant finances that advance and is repaid from later municipal power surcharges.
The Commerce temple can certify weight and title for insurers and place a hold mark, but its mark does not own the Hold's civic release decision.
Mana-eating mould is an established specialized ecological response to industrial pressure, while its interpretation remains politically disputed.

ambient_pressures.text: The same crystal contracts support water, kitchens, lifts, and district heat, so withholding or spending reserves changes ordinary life before it changes company profit.
A roll offer can keep one wagon and a mine payroll moving while replacing today's call with senior claims against deeper future production.
Workshop seals own public policy, but physical rail movement, temple insurance, creditor appetite, company payroll, and resident trust remain independent pressure surfaces.

groups.label: Brasswater Reserve House
institutional_logic: Execute the sealed reserve charter, keep emergency stock attributable, and publish the service-days gauge.
material_incentives: Keep water, kitchens, lifts, and heat operating while preserving enough credit and future supply to refill the cells.
internal_shames: An empty cell presented as prudence
A charter stretched by one keeper
A ration imposed without a ledger
prestige_markers: A disputed load segregated and traceable
A wider moot arriving with evidence attached
taboo_triggers: Treating the public gauge as confidential
Letting creditor or insurer advice become an unrecorded command
emotional_display_norms: Fear is translated into counts, thresholds, release orders, ration schedules, and dry jokes about paperwork.
trust_defaults: Trusts witnessed stores, signed ledgers, physical custody, and workshops that accept named obligations.

groups.label: Deep Company contract interest
institutional_logic: Keep shafts financed, wagons sold, payroll current, and emergency clauses narrow enough to preserve export revenue.
material_incentives: Avoid a full foreign breach, retain future municipal business, and refinance today's valid call through deeper production.
internal_shames: A valid call treated as theft only after accepting its advance
prestige_markers: A cargo kept inside insurable language
A deeper shaft with committed buyers
taboo_triggers: Public reading of private escape clauses
Worker custody of the switch key
A hold that makes the export clock visible
emotional_display_norms: Panic is compressed into options, schedules, disaster categories, and concern for payroll.
trust_defaults: Trusts enforceable terms and customers already dependent on delivery more than moral appeals.

groups.label: Commerce-temple assay and insurance interest
institutional_logic: Make weight, title, hazard, and insurable custody legible without claiming the civic power to spend the cargo.
material_incentives: Avoid underwriting an unpriced ecological loss while keeping temple treasuries and warrant holdings credible.
internal_virtues: A hold narrower than a confiscation
internal_shames: Blessing title that cannot survive audit
Using divine language to hide an insurer's limit
Letting an ash mark masquerade as civic command
prestige_markers: A claim paid from a clean chain
An assay both company and Hold must cite
A temple mark that remains narrow under pressure
taboo_triggers: Calling unresolved hazard harmless for political convenience
Forcing the temple to insure a release it did not classify
emotional_display_norms: Concern appears as calibrated ritual, measured language, and refusal to broaden a mark beyond its evidence.
trust_defaults: Trusts witnessed assay, clean title, and named liability; distrusts both company self-certification and unrecorded emergency improvisation.

groups.label: Rail workers and protected-service workshops
institutional_logic: Keep cargo movement physically safe and keep public decisions attached to the workers and residents who bear failure.
material_incentives: Protect wages and bodies while keeping pumps, kitchens, lifts, and heat supplied.
internal_virtues: Service costs stated in household terms
internal_shames: Moving unsafe cargo under cover of legality
Demanding purity from households while someone else loses heat
Letting the company divide mine payroll from municipal labour
prestige_markers: A route kept open without hiding the cost
A petition that brings the right workshops into the moot
taboo_triggers: Treating workers as automatic motion after a seal is stamped
Calling resident testimony an obstacle to technical policy
emotional_display_norms: Anger appears as held controls, collective positioning, exact failure descriptions, and humor sharpened by familiarity with machinery.
trust_defaults: Trusts visible safeguards, public ledgers, crew testimony, and decision-makers who share the ration cost.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: A keeper may act quickly only because the charter, stock, threshold, and protected schedules are visible enough for affected workshops to contest afterward.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Prompt Brasswater actors to state what the gauge protects, show the physical cargo state, and widen authority when the charter itself must change.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: The company converts a valid emergency claim into a choice between current breach and future dependence on deeper production.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Company characters should offer concrete wagons, delivery dates, liens, and payroll consequences instead of abstract pro-industry speeches.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: The temple gains legitimacy by keeping assay, hold, insurance, and civic release distinct even when every faction wants its mark to decide more.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Temple dialogue should name exactly what is weighed, held, or uninsured and refuse authority beyond that scope.

observer_read: A frightened municipal buyer manufacturing an emergency to seize a high-value shipment
A future customer who will return once its cells empty
target_self_read: A chartered public workshop executing a prepaid call while exposing its own future debt
misread_patterns: Underestimates the keeper's need to widen authority
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Let Yorrin correctly identify Brasswater's future supply weakness while misreading public visibility as mere leverage theater.

observer_read: A company using wages and export penalties as shields for a hazardous load
A contract office that discovers workers only when payroll is threatened
target_self_read: The institution keeping both mines and public infrastructure supplied through difficult conditions
misread_patterns: Workers may flatten real mine payroll dependence into executive greed
Company staff may treat refusal as sabotage rather than safety authority
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Keep Dori's suspicion material and allow the company payroll consequence to remain real rather than becoming a rhetorical trick.

observer_read: An insurer using sacred scales to avoid sharing a public risk
target_self_read: A witness preserving honest weight and bounded liability so later claims remain payable
misread_patterns: Civic urgency can treat a narrow insurance refusal as moral abandonment
Temple caution can understate the bodily cost of delay
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Use the tension to separate assay truth from release authority without making either side foolish.

role_pressure_fields.summary: A workshop Master able to execute an emergency charter but unable to erase the independent authority of workers, insurers, creditors, companies, or affected seals.
obligations: Widen jurisdiction when changing the charter
available_masks: Humor used to keep fear from owning the room
failure_modes: Letting emergency execution become private policy
Securing cargo without a shared account
Signing future debt because it ends today's noise

role_pressure_fields.summary: A worker representative whose crews physically own safe movement but do not own the reserve charter.
obligations: Refuse orders that make labour hide the risk
failure_modes: Turning a safety hold into unaccountable seizure
Letting solidarity become an invisible veto

role_pressure_fields.summary: A practical priest and insurer witness who can assay, mark, and refuse coverage but cannot make the civic release decision.
obligations: Name what the temple will not insure
failure_modes: Letting an ash mark become political custody
Hiding an insurer's interest inside revelation
Delaying until the public cost becomes invisible

role_pressure_fields.summary: A contract negotiator who carries real mine wages and export penalties into the room while trying to turn a called debt into deeper future leverage.
failure_modes: Binding the Hold to a deeper unsafe site
Losing control of the emergency definition

known_context.text: Lysa knows Brasswater's charter, stock, service gauge, warrant obligations, call-right, local rail geometry, and the authority attached to her workshop seal.

beliefs.text: Lysa believes emergency action remains legitimate only while its threshold, custody, and later costs can be inspected and contested.

misreads.text: She may underestimate how quickly a missed company payroll or foreign breach can break future supply cooperation.

must_not_know.text: Lysa must not know whether mould contamination expresses one dungeon mind, distributed adaptation, local accident, or a mixture.

known_context.text: Dori knows the brake line, switch path, crew roster, cell access, and what moving a doubtful load asks workers to touch.

beliefs.text: Dori believes a seal can authorize movement but cannot make an unsafe operation physically honest.

misreads.text: She may treat Yorrin's payroll argument as pure hostage-taking even when a real mine shift will lose wages.

must_not_know.text: Dori must not know the company's directors' private tolerance for breach unless Yorrin reveals it through terms or action.

known_context.text: Sava knows the assay result, temple marks, insurer conditions, warrant exposure, and the distinction between hold, condemnation, release, and coverage.

beliefs.text: Sava believes narrow public marks protect both religious credibility and payable claims under pressure.

misreads.text: She may underweight the bodily cost of delay because a clean claims boundary remains valuable after tonight's ration has passed.

must_not_know.text: Sava must not turn the assay into divine proof of planetary pain or innocence.

known_context.text: Yorrin knows the call-right, export penalty, mine payroll, prepared roll, and disaster clauses he is authorized to offer.

beliefs.text: Yorrin believes uninterrupted contracts and financed production are the only mechanisms large enough to keep current infrastructure supplied.

misreads.text: He may mistake visible public process for negotiable theater and underestimate workers' refusal or the widening franchise.

must_not_know.text: Yorrin must not know that the deeper site can safely satisfy the rolled calls; the setting makes that uncertainty material.

author_only_boundaries.text: The fixture dramatizes a representative Brasswater call hearing. None of its eight branch endings is canonical event history unless separately promoted.
The mana-eating mould is source-grounded, but its presence on this shipment does not prove a single dungeon, god, or World-Spirit intentionally contaminated the load.
Commerce-temple insurance practice is a political-economic elaboration, not a resolution of which gods precede or depend on worship.

open_questions.question: How widely do Commerce temples share claims procedures and insurer networks between Holds?
open_questions.notes: This fixture needs only one local weigh-priest and outside claim path. Broader temple standardization belongs to a future Numen or Tangle pass if it recurs.

open_questions.question: Which foreign buyer and human realm holds the interrupted export contract?
open_questions.notes: The local hearing requires a real export penalty but not a new realm. A future Tangle pass can connect the contract after the human political map gains a suitable existing owner.
